### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 74a19dd857d5b7bddd8409bd04332cc10c6ad5ae` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0b058828e0b0b5ea417f9e9baf8a5d3317578835` — the merge of head `791e47c3443134c115160aa63e50264152cd19de` into base `74a19dd857d5b7bddd8409bd04332cc10c6ad5ae`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0b058828e0b0b5ea417f9e9baf8a5d3317578835 && git checkout 0b058828e0b0b5ea417f9e9baf8a5d3317578835
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 74a19dd857d5b7bddd8409bd04332cc10c6ad5ae 791e47c3443134c115160aa63e50264152cd19de && git checkout -B drift-repro 74a19dd857d5b7bddd8409bd04332cc10c6ad5ae && git merge --no-ff 791e47c3443134c115160aa63e50264152cd19de

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 74a19dd857d5b7bddd8409bd04332cc10c6ad5ae
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `791e47c3443134c115160aa63e50264152cd19de`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/create-objectstack/src/index.ts, packages/create-objectstack/src/template-copy.ts, packages/create-objectstack/src/scaffold-current-dir-collision.test.ts + packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/ (the template tree the walk reads, incl. `_gitignore`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `src/`), packages/create-objectstack/src/index.ts `topLevelNames` / `writeIfAbsent` / `rewriteProjectIdentity` (the other writers of the run), packages/create-objectstack/src/rewrite-identity.ts, packages/create-objectstack/src/runtime-image.ts, packages/create-objectstack/src/scaffold-description.test.ts (the `tsx` pattern the new test copies), packages/create-objectstack/package.json (`exports`), .changeset/29134-current-dir-overwrite-refusal.md (read for ②), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (`CATEGORIES`). Remainder of the diff at TIER_DEFAULT: none — the narrowing face's floor covers every non-prose path; the changeset is judged in ② only.

Inputs read: card #29134 body + all 3 comments (triage 6572501857, claim 6574098591, dev report 6575170911); PR #29267 body, file list (4 files, +249/−6), net diff `origin/main...791e47c3`; check-runs on `791e47c3` (final tally below). Reviewed 2026-11-02T10:58Z.

### ① Derived judgments

- **CLI behaviour (public surface of `create-objectstack`)** — a no-name / `""` run in a current directory where a template file already exists now exits 1 and writes nothing; on `main` it exited 0 and replaced the files. Narrowing, declared `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset. **Right.** Read in the tree: the check sits inside the `try`, after the unchanged named-dir refusal and the `targetWasEmpty` snapshot, before `fs.mkdirSync` and `loadBundled` — nothing is written before `process.exit(1)`.
- **Scoped-to-collisions rule, not blanket non-empty refusal** — a current dir holding only `.git/`, `notes.txt`, or a user-populated `src/` without template-named files still scaffolds. **Right**: it matches the card's "Expected" (refuse to overwrite existing files, naming them) and the claim's expected shape; the `targetWasEmpty` short-circuit keeps the empty-dir path byte-identical to `main`.
- **No new accept-set**: `findTemplateCollisions` is a new export of `src/template-copy.ts`, which `package.json#exports` does not expose (only `./created-summary`); the `bin` is the sole public entry. **Right** — no published API surface added, no `check:api-surface` owed.
- **`copyDir` refactor** (`outputName` shared) — behaviour-neutral: same `isFile()`-gated alias lookup. **Right.** The two walks share the alias rule, so `_gitignore` is checked and written as `.gitignore` (unit test pins it).
- **Other writers of the run are covered or exclusive-create** — every `writeFileSync`/`copyFileSync` outside the copy writes a template file (`rewriteProjectIdentity` → package.json / manifest / config / README; `rewrite-identity.ts`; `runtime-image.ts` → Dockerfile) or goes through `writeIfAbsent` (`flag: 'wx'`: AGENTS.md, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`). The PR body's acceptance note is accurate against the tree. `<pm> install` and the skills installer write their own trees, as before — out of the card's reach.
- **Claim boundary** — no `packages/spec/**`, no new CLI flag, no new gate: **holds** on the file list.
- **Prose** — `packages/create-objectstack/README.md` ("Scaffold in the current directory") and `content/docs` stay true: the current-dir path still scaffolds unless it would overwrite. Docs Drift check listed nothing. No drift.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29134-current-dir-overwrite-refusal.md`: `'create-objectstack': patch`, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body. **Correct level**: `Metadata-protocol: none` ⇒ `patch`; a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). Not `skip-changeset` — the package publishes.
- ADR-0087 marker: `<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) … -->` — `no-migration-prescription` is in `CATEGORIES` of `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`; nothing an author writes is removed or renamed (no schema key, no export, no config field), so no tombstone and no FROM → TO mapping is owed. The remedy line is present. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.
- `Clause-②:` line — `no (narrowing)`: **right**. On the measured case exit 0 → exit 1 with nothing written; nothing widened; the `(narrowing)` arm is the one that makes this review owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_question 1 — `--force` opt-in to overwrite? **Answered: A (no flag).** The claim's file surface forbids a new CLI flag; the remedy is a `mv` or a named directory, both printed by the refusal. Option B is a product choice and stays a maintainer question, not a blocker on this card.
- open_question 2 — new sentence `Directory is not empty and the template would overwrite N existing files: DIR`, no error code in this CLI? **Answered: A (land as worded).** It keeps the existing "Directory … not empty" lead, adds the count, lists each path, and says nothing was written; the test pins the count and both path lines.
- deviation: harness attribution block on PR lines 1–2, `Fixes #29134` on line 3 — accepted (os-dev harness exception).
- deviation: no MCP assignee/reviewer write — accepted; the standard order forbids MCP writes.
- deviation: dogfood ran in the background while gates ran unlocked; three gates first exited 3 on prerequisites and re-ran green — accepted; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts here, and they are green.
- Nothing escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/create-objectstack/src/template-copy.ts` — `findTemplateCollisions`.** Judged against `copyDir` (the writer it must predict) and the `blank` template tree on the head. The walk is `readdirSync(src, withFileTypes)` → `outputName` → `lstatSync(dest/outName)`, recursing only where both sides are directories; a file where the template needs a directory is a collision; a template file over any existing entry is a collision; absent entries are skipped. Tried to break it: (a) `_gitignore` vs a user `.gitignore` — caught via the shared alias (unit test). (b) User `.github/` holding other workflows — walked, no false positive unless `workflows/ci.yml` exists; the later `writeIfAbsent` for copilot-instructions keeps the user's copy. (c) A symlink standing where the template writes — `lstatSync` sees it, so it is a collision; `copyFileSync` would have written through it, so conservative is right. (d) A file named `src` — caught; without the check `copyDir`'s `mkdirSync('src')` would have thrown ENOTDIR mid-copy, leaving a half-written tree, so the pre-check is strictly better than the previous failure mode. (e) Case-insensitive filesystems — a user `readme.md` is seen by `lstatSync` as colliding with `README.md`, which is exactly what the copy would have overwritten; the printed name is the template's, acceptable. No must-fix.

**`packages/create-objectstack/src/index.ts` — the refusal block.** Placement: after the unchanged `!isCurrentDir` refusal and the `targetWasEmpty` read, inside the `try`, before `mkdirSync`/`loadBundled`. A thrown `readdirSync`/`bundledTemplateDir` error is caught by the existing `catch` → `printError` → exit 1, same as the pre-change `loadBundled` throw. `targetWasEmpty` (`topLevelNames` returns an empty set for a missing dir) short-circuits the walk for the empty and not-yet-existing cases, so the named-dir and empty-current-dir paths run no new code. The named-dir non-empty refusal still fires first, so its message is unchanged (test pins it). `bundledTemplateDir` extracted from `loadBundled` without changing the "missing on disk" throw. No must-fix. One note, not a finding: the sentence says "overwrite N existing files" even when an entry is a file blocking a template directory — the count and list are still correct, and the alternative outcome on `main` was an ENOTDIR crash halfway, so the wording is at worst slightly generous.

**`packages/create-objectstack/src/scaffold-current-dir-collision.test.ts`.** Judged against the card's reproduction and the scenario it is accepted against. It spawns the real CLI through `tsx` (the `scaffold-description.test.ts` pattern, `index.ts` parses on import), with `--template blank --skip-install --skip-skills`. The two refusal cases (no name, `""`) assert exit 1, a whole-tree byte snapshot unchanged, the count line, both colliding paths as their own lines, the non-colliding `notes.txt` absent from the list, and no "Environment created!". The non-colliding case (`.git/HEAD` + `notes.txt`) asserts exit 0, the "already had contents" summary, `package.json` name from the directory, and both user files byte-identical. The empty-dir and named-non-empty cases pin the unchanged paths. Three unit cases pin the alias, the file-where-directory case, and the shared-`src/` no-collision case. The dev's ablation (anchor `if (collisions.length > 0) {` removed → the two refusal cases red with `expected +0 to be 1`) is consistent with the test shape; I did not re-run it. Coverage gap worth naming, should-fix (non-blocking): no test asserts the `--template` lookup still precedes the collision walk for a template that is retired/unknown — but only `blank` exists in `src/templates/`, so the case is unreachable on this tree. No must-fix.

**Narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** It takes no declared capability away: scaffolding into the current directory remains available whenever it would not replace a user file; it makes the spec's own refusal ("Directory already exists and is not empty", previously named-dir only) real on the current-dir path, scoped to the files that would actually be lost. The card's "Expected" is met in its first form (refuse to overwrite existing files, naming the files it would replace).

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none blocking (one coverage note above).

Check-runs on `791e47c3` (all complete at read time): 50 total — 36 success, 14 skipped (UI, docs, opt-in and schedule lanes with no paths hit), 0 failure/cancelled/neutral. Green among them: Test Core (8/8 shards + aggregate), TypeScript Type Check (workspace, source gates, debt ledger, consumer gates), Lint & Repo Gates (ESLint, repo & tooling, docs & code guards, CI/release/engine gates, PM dispatch-gates, scoped lanes), Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Scaffold with repo dist, Build Core. These conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was re-run locally.
